brief: Goldman maintains its base case that continued Mideast supply adaptation eventually lowers crude prices, while renewed escalation remains a net upside risk. It raises its Brent Dec26 forecast to $90 (from $85) because slower-than-expected moderation in the oil risk premium (near $20/bbl) offsets faster Gulf supply recovery. The 2027 Brent forecast stays at $80, balancing those two forces. WTI is forecast at $81 Dec26 and $73 2027. Persian Gulf exports, including an estimated 4mb/d of dark exports, have recovered to roughly their 2025 average since late September, and the global market was nearly balanced in September (0.3mb/d deficit vs 7.2mb/d in March). Despite the recovery, physical prices stay high because escalation risk to oil infrastructure and low global inventories are driving restocking and hedging demand. Goldman raised its September fair-value estimate by $6 to $80. The base case still sees a 2026Q4-2027 surplus, as 2026Q3 global demand ran 3.3mb/d below last year, partly from Hormuz-linked demand destruction. Historically, supply shocks last 4.5 years and cut regional output sharply, keeping risks skewed to the upside. Goldman recommends long summer-2027 European gasoline, call options over outright crude length for investors, and put spreads for producers hedging downside.
